assessment.nobel_worthiness: A foundational, broad body of political-economy research linking political institutions, state capacity, electoral incentives and fiscal policy to economic development.
assessment.attribution: Besley, Persson and Tabellini are central and complementary contributors to the modern analytical framework, though the intellectual field has many relevant contributors.
assessment.maturity: The work has shaped research and policy analysis over decades and its importance is well established.
uncertainties: The breadth of the contribution makes a three-person attribution necessarily selective.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population-scale evidence on intergenerational mobility has changed how economists measure equality of opportunity and evaluate place-based policy.
assessment.attribution: Chetty and Hendren are especially central to the mobility research program, with Friedman a major contributor to its administrative-data infrastructure and empirical implementation.
assessment.maturity: The empirical approach has been extensively adopted and its policy relevance is already substantial.
uncertainties: The long-run causal interpretation of geographic mobility correlations remains an active research question.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Audit and correspondence designs have produced compelling evidence on discrimination and materially improved empirical approaches to unequal treatment in labour markets.
assessment.attribution: Bertrand and Mullainathan made a landmark audit-study contribution; Charles is an important contributor to the wider labour-discrimination literature.
assessment.maturity: The methods are widely replicated, adapted and influential beyond labour economics.
uncertainties: Audit-study estimates identify particular margins of discrimination and do not alone summarize all mechanisms of labour-market inequality.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The reconstruction of long-run income and wealth inequality transformed the empirical basis for studying distribution, taxation and wealth concentration.
assessment.attribution: Piketty and Saez established core distributional series, while Zucman made major contributions on wealth measurement and offshore assets.
assessment.maturity: The research has generated a durable international data infrastructure and a large scholarly literature.
uncertainties: Historical and offshore-wealth estimates require consequential measurement and capitalization assumptions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Their work supplied influential economic frameworks for exhaustible resources, biodiversity and the treatment of natural capital in social welfare.
assessment.attribution: Dasgupta and Heal are central early architects of the named resource and inclusive-wealth contributions.
assessment.maturity: These ideas have had a long intellectual gestation and growing practical relevance as biodiversity and sustainability measurement advance.
uncertainties: Operational measurement of biodiversity and inclusive wealth remains incomplete and contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Research on monopsony has revised understanding of wage setting, employer power and the incidence of labour-market policy.
assessment.attribution: Manning supplied a central theoretical synthesis, while Naidu and Ashenfelter made important empirical and institutional contributions.
assessment.maturity: The framework has become highly influential in contemporary labour economics and policy debate.
uncertainties: The empirical magnitude and sources of employer power vary substantially across settings.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The misallocation framework provided a tractable and influential account of how distorted input allocation can affect aggregate productivity and international income gaps.
assessment.attribution: Hsieh, Klenow and Restuccia are leading contributors to the associated measurement and quantitative framework.
assessment.maturity: The approach has prompted extensive theoretical, empirical and policy-oriented work across countries.
uncertainties: Measured wedges need not map cleanly onto specific policy distortions or causal mechanisms.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Evolutionary accounts of routines, organizational learning and firm dynamics have been deeply influential in understanding economic change outside equilibrium models.
assessment.attribution: Winter is an indispensable originator of this research tradition, although its development also involved important collaborators and successors.
assessment.maturity: The contribution has endured for decades across organizational economics, strategy and innovation research.
uncertainties: Its diffuse, interdisciplinary influence makes the appropriate Nobel citation and boundary less straightforward.
